transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what brought me in is... I just can't stop jumping out of my skin lately. 

I do maintenance work, and if a breaker snaps loud or a guy drops a tool on the concrete, I practically jump out of my boots. Same thing if somebody just comes up behind me without me seeing them first. My heart starts hammering in my chest, and... it just keeps pounding, long after everyone else has just moved on and gone back to work. It's getting really bad, to be honest.
Did these symptoms begin after a specific distressing or life-threatening event that you experienced?
Yeah, they did. Uh... there was an arc-flash accident on this retrofit job I was working. That was about a year and a month ago now, and... yeah, this has been going on ever since then.
Do you find yourself having unwanted memories or dreams about that arc-flash accident?

Yeah, I do. It happens... out of nowhere, really. I could just be loading tools in the truck, minding my own business, and suddenly I'll see that flash in my head. Or I'll hear the trainee yelling. It just knocks me sideways, you know? Like it's happening all over again right then and there.
Do you find yourself going out of your way to avoid places, people, or situations that remind you of that accident?

Yeah, I definitely do. I... I find myself making excuses not to go near certain panels or breakers anymore. Or even certain job sites, really. And I definitely don't want to talk about that day with anybody. I just avoid it all. Because... well, once that stuff starts playing in my head, I just can't shut it off. So it's just easier to stay away.
Since that accident, have you noticed that your overall outlook on life or your feelings about other people have changed?

Yeah, they have. I just... I walk around mad all the time now. And guilty. I just feel this heavy guilt, like I failed that trainee kid, you know? It's just there, all the time. I feel like everybody can see it on me, too. Like they know.
When you have these sudden memories of the accident, do you feel like you are actually reliving the event as if it is happening again right now, rather than just remembering it?

No, I wouldn't say I'm actually reliving it. I mean... I know I'm not back at that site. It's just a really intense memory that hits me out of nowhere, and it messes with my head for a minute. But I still know I'm standing by my truck, or wherever I happen to be, you know? I don't lose track of where I actually am, if that's what you mean.
